recent_articles.title: Renowned infectious diseases expert Dr Naseem Salahuddin passes away - Pakistan - DAWN.COM

recent_articles.title: Ebola risk raised to 'very high' in DR Congo

recent_articles.title: RO systems should be maintained properly to be effective, says study - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: A recent study in Chennai, India, found that while **reverse osmosis (RO)** systems effectively remove microbes under ideal conditions, they are not a guarantee for safe drinking water. The study, published in the Journal of Exposure Science & Environmental Epidemiology, revealed that 31% of post-RO samples still contained **Escherichia coli** (E. coli), compared to 71% in untreated water.  The researchers found a correlation between education level and E. coli contamination, with higher levels of education associated with lower rates of contamination. The study emphasizes the need for proper maintenance and hygiene practices alongside reliable piped water supply and affordable servicing structures to ensure safe drinking water access.

recent_articles.title: Melanoma skin cancer cases in UK hit record level, analysis finds | Skin cancer | The Guardian
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Cancer Research UK** has reported a record high of 20,980 melanoma cases in the UK for 2022, with projections suggesting that by 2040 there could be 26,500 new cases annually. The charity attributes the increase to the UK's growing and ageing population, and emphasizes that most cases are preventable through sun safety measures like seeking shade, covering up, and using sunscreen. **Fiona Osgun**, head of health information at **Cancer Research UK**, advises protecting skin from UV damage even on cooler or cloudier days. **Prof Peter Johnson**, national clinical director for cancer at **NHS England**, stresses the importance of sensible sun exposure practices to prevent melanoma, urging individuals to seek medical attention if they notice any unusual changes in their skin.

recent_articles.title: Ebola outbreak in DR Congo: Angry crowd sets Rwampara hospital tents on fire
recent_articles.rephrased_article: An angry crowd in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo set fire to hospital tents used for Ebola isolation wards, after the death of a young man who was thought to have died from typhoid fever but whose body was not allowed to be buried. **Luc Malembe Malembe**, a local politician, witnessed the scene and stated that people did not believe the virus existed. recent_articles.title: Qatar-based British-Pakistani scientist develops AI eye scan for early dementia diagnosis - World - DAWN.COM
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Professor Rayaz Malik**, a British-Pakistani scientist based in Qatar, has developed an AI-powered eye scan using corneal confocal microscopy (CCM) that can detect dementia and diabetic nerve damage years before symptoms appear.  This technology, traditionally used to diagnose infections and abnormalities in the front surface of the eye, has been shown to identify microscopic nerve fibre damage associated with diseases such as diabetes, chemotherapy, inflammatory disorders, and infectious diseases. **Professor Malik** believes this could be particularly important for countries facing ageing populations and rising rates of neurological disease.  The technology's ability to detect early-stage cognitive decline could lead to more effective treatments and earlier interventions.

recent_articles.title: Bihar midday meal incident: HC asks whether NGO can continue providing meals - The Hindu

recent_articles.title: Patient tests HIV-positive after surgery, triggering probe at Multan’s Nishtar Hospital - Pakistan - DAWN.COM

recent_articles.title: Ebola: US ban on travellers from DRC, Uganda or South Sudan ‘not the solution’ | Global development | The Guardian

recent_articles.title: Autoimmune diseases higher than before; long-term effect of pesticides need to be studied: expert - The Hindu

recent_articles.title: Gonorrhoea and syphilis hit record levels in Europe, data shows

recent_articles.title: Scientists turn sheep wool into a bone-healing material in a major medical breakthrough | - The Times of India

While further testing is needed before human trials, researchers believe this sustainable source of biomaterials could revolutionize bone repair and dental reconstruction.

recent_articles.title: New Mexico Substance Exposure: Mystery substance scare in New Mexico: 3 dead, first responders quarantined over toxic exposure - The Times of India

recent_articles.title: Canada faces calls for investigation into death of woman after plasma donation | Canada | The Guardian
recent_articles.rephrased_article: Patient advocates are calling for a new investigation into the death of Rodiyat Alabede, a young woman who died after donating plasma in Winnipeg.  **Health Canada** initially found no link between her death and the donation, but campaigners allege significant discrepancies between the autopsy report and the agency's medical summary. **Grifols**, the company that operated the facility where Alabede donated, has acknowledged issues with staff training and reporting, but maintains it is working to address them. recent_articles.title: ‘Research here is world class’: son of Steve Jobs looks to invest in UK cancer care | Venture capital | The Guardian

recent_articles.title: Hantavirus outbreak: Deadly Andes strain detected in cruise ship cases; eight cases confirmed - The Times of India

recent_articles.title: Australians from hantavirus cruise ship to fly out of Netherlands in full PPE after plane and crew secured | Hantavirus | The Guardian

recent_articles.title: Hantavirus: After hantavirus, now norovirus? How a gut bug forced a France cruise ship into lockdown - The Times of India

recent_articles.title: JD Vance threatens health funding to states that don’t comply with White House anti-fraud effort | US healthcare | The Guardian

recent_articles.title: Drug overdose deaths drop in United States for third year in a row | Drugs News | Al Jazeera
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The United States Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)** released data showing a nearly 14 percent decline in drug overdose deaths in 2025, reaching nearly 70,000. This marks the third consecutive year of declining overdose deaths, attributed to factors such as increased availability of naloxone, fentanyl testing strips, and regulatory changes in China limiting access to fentanyl-making chemicals. While the trend is positive, seven states saw increases in overdose deaths.  President Donald Trump's administration has highlighted the decrease as a sign of success for its crackdown on drug trafficking, while experts have criticized such claims as exaggerated.

recent_articles.title: 'No indication' Andes strain of hantavirus has mutated: EU agency - World - DAWN.COM
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control (ECDC)** stated that there is no evidence suggesting the Andes strain of hantavirus has mutated following a deadly outbreak on a cruise ship. **Andreas Hoefer**, a microbiologist from the ECDC, explained preliminary genome sequencing data indicates a single transmission event from an infected animal to humans.  **The World Health Organisation (WHO)** recommends a 42-day quarantine and constant monitoring for high-risk contacts due to the long incubation period of six weeks.

recent_articles.title: Pakistan, WHO launch Prime Minister's Hepatitis C Elimination Programme - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Pakistan** and the **World Health Organization (WHO)** launched the Prime Minister’s Hepatitis C Elimination Programme in Islamabad. The program aims to eliminate hepatitis C as a public health threat by 2030, with an initial focus on screening and treatment for 1.6 million people over six months.  The initiative will provide free three-to-six month treatment courses for all patients. **Federal Health Minister Mustafa Kamal** emphasized the importance of prevention and early intervention in combating the disease, which affects nearly 10 million Pakistanis. The program is supported by the **National Database and Registration Authority (Nadra)** to ensure nationwide screening using national database integration.

recent_articles.title: Woman isolating on British island in South Pacific after hantavirus contact
recent_articles.rephrased_article: A woman who traveled on a hantavirus-hit cruise ship is currently isolating on the Pitcairn Islands after contact with an infected individual. The **UK foreign office** and **UKHSA** are coordinating with local authorities to manage risks, while the **WHO** has confirmed nine cases of the virus, including two suspected.  The woman's isolation is expected to last 45 days as a precaution, but she will not be allowed to re-enter French Polynesia due to potential risk to others. The **French Polynesian government** stated that passengers on the same flight from San Francisco to Tahiti are not considered close contacts and the risk of infection is low.

recent_articles.title: France confines over 1,700 passengers on cruise ship over gastroenteritis | Health News | Al Jazeera
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **French** authorities have temporarily restricted the disembarkation of 1,233 passengers and 514 crew members on a British cruise ship docked in Bordeaux after nearly 50 suspected cases of gastroenteritis were reported. The **Ambition**, carrying mostly British or Irish nationals, had travelled from Belfast and Liverpool before arriving in southwestern France on Tuesday evening. Cruise operator **Ambassador Cruise Line** has introduced enhanced sanitation measures and offered full refunds to affected passengers. Health officials are conducting medical tests to determine the cause of the outbreak, which is not believed to be linked to a hantavirus cluster reported on another ship.

recent_articles.title: More than 1,000 passengers held on cruise after gastrointestinal illness outbreak
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Ambassador Cruise Line** is operating a UK-operated cruise ship, the Ambition, in France after 49 passengers fell ill with gastrointestinal illness. **Local health authorities** have suspended passenger disembarkations and dispatched a medical team to assess the situation.  The cruise line has implemented enhanced sanitation protocols and reported that 48 passengers and one crew member are displaying symptoms consistent with gastrointestinal illness. The cause of death for a 92-year-old man who passed away on board is yet to be determined.

recent_articles.title: Hantavirus outbreak: Passengers evacuated from cruise ship to leave hospital after 72-hour quarantine - The Times of India
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Passengers** evacuated from the virus-hit Dutch cruise ship MV Hondius are set to begin leaving a specialist isolation facility in the UK after completing an initial 72-hour quarantine period.  All passengers remain healthy and asymptomatic, but will continue self-isolation at home for another 42 days as a precaution. The **UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA)** stated that public health specialists will assess whether individuals can safely isolate at home or if alternative accommodation arrangements are necessary. The outbreak aboard the expedition cruise ship has so far been linked to three deaths, including two confirmed hantavirus cases.  The WHO has confirmed six infections linked to the outbreak, with more potential cases still possible.

recent_articles.title: The class politics of modern outbreaks | Health | Al Jazeera
recent_articles.rephrased_article: A recent hantavirus outbreak on the MV Hondius, a luxury cruise ship, highlights concerns about elite mobility and its impact on global health. The outbreak, which has led to confirmed cases and deaths, underscores the unequal distribution of risks associated with disease transmission during pandemics.  While wealthy passengers often travel freely and experience minimal consequences, poorer populations in regions where outbreaks occur bear the brunt of the risk. This pattern reflects a larger issue of inequality within globalization, where wealthier individuals contribute disproportionately to the spread of diseases while those with fewer resources are most vulnerable to their effects.

recent_articles.title: London prisoner with muscle-wasting condition claims he has to crawl on floor | UK news | The Guardian
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Umer Khalid**, a prisoner at Wormwood Scrubs awaiting trial for alleged involvement in a break-in at RAF Brize Norton, claims he has been forced to crawl due to inadequate medical care and lack of a wheelchair. **Khalid**, who suffers from limb-girdle muscular dystrophy, alleges that prison officials have ignored his needs, including missed appointments with healthcare professionals and insufficient access to medication and high protein food. He also claims to have been left in his cell during a fire alarm evacuation and denied proper treatment for his condition despite being diagnosed with muscular dystrophy in 2014. **Shabana Khalid**, his mother, expressed outrage at the prison's response, stating that her son is suffering from severe physical deterioration.

recent_articles.title: Inquest into death of Clare Nowland after Tasering by NSW police aims to answer ‘outstanding questions’ | New South Wales | The Guardian
recent_articles.rephrased_article: An inquest into the death of 95-year-old Clare Nowland, who died after being Tasered by **Constable Kristian James Samuel White** at Yallambee Lodge nursing home in Cooma, is expected to focus on improving training for first responders dealing with aggressive dementia patients. The three-day inquest will examine systemic issues related to dementia care and training for aged care staff, police, and ambulance officers, as well as the communication between these groups.  State coroner Teresa O’Sullivan will examine whether Nowland's care was reasonable and if there were any contributing factors that led to her death.

recent_articles.title: Free vaccination for cervical cancer until May 31 - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **District Collector G. Priyanka** announced the final phase of the HPV vaccination campaign against cervical cancer in the district, urging all eligible girls to receive the vaccine before May 31, 2026.  The campaign aims to vaccinate a total of 22,358 girls aged 14 and under, with only 34% currently vaccinated as of the current date. The vaccination facility will cease operation after this deadline.

recent_articles.title: Older people risk mental decline if they do long hours of caring, UK study shows | Carers | The Guardian
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Carers UK** and researchers at **University College London** have found that providing care for 5 to 9 hours a week can boost brain health, while long hours of care lead to accelerated cognitive decline. The study compared the cognitive health of 2,765 carers aged 50 or over with 2,765 non-carers and found that those providing more than 50 hours of care experienced faster mental decline.  The researchers suggest that the government should provide more support for "intensive" carers through better access to funded formal and replacement care. The findings highlight the need for increased support for family caregivers who often face significant stress and burnout.

recent_articles.title: Metal screw removed from baby’s lung at Government Chengalpattu Medical College Hospital - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Doctors** at the **Government Chengalpattu Medical College Hospital** successfully removed a small metal screw from the right lung of a one-year-old girl who presented with breathing difficulties. The procedure, performed by a team led by associate professor of paediatrics **Sarath Balaji**, involved a minimally invasive bronchoscope and forceps. The child has since recovered and is doing well.

recent_articles.title: WHO chief says 'work not over' after hantavirus evacuation - World - DAWN.COM
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **WHO** chief Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus stated that the global public health risk from the hantavirus outbreak on the cruise ship **MV Hondius** is low, but the situation could change.  He emphasized the need for continued monitoring and highlighted the importance of following WHO guidelines, including quarantine measures. While some countries adopted different approaches to handling returning evacuees, **WHO** officials urged adherence to their recommendations.

recent_articles.title: Capacity of lifts not kept up with UK obesity levels, study shows | Obesity | The Guardian
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Researchers** have found that **lifts** in the UK and mainland Europe are no longer large enough to accommodate the increasing weight of adults, raising concerns about safety and equity. A study presented at the European Congress on Obesity found that maximum lift capacities haven't increased since around 2004 despite average adult weights rising significantly. The research suggests manufacturers have focused on floor space rather than weight, failing to account for the increase in obesity rates. **Prof Nick Finer**, president of the International Prader-Willi Syndrome Organisation and lead author of the study, emphasized that this issue impacts not only safety but also social inclusion by creating stigma for individuals with obesity.

recent_articles.title: Pakistan to face growing health risk as international funding to health sector continues to decline: report - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Pakistan** faces serious health risks due to declining international funding for its healthcare sector.  A report by the think tank Tabadlab warns that cuts in Official Development Assistance (ODA) could lead to disruptions in disease control programs, immunisation efforts, and institutional capacity across the country. The report highlights a sharp decline in global ODA flows since 2019, with total funding dropping from $215 billion in 2024 to $174.3 billion in 2025.  The report emphasizes the need for Pakistan to reduce its reliance on external health financing and strengthen domestic systems before further aid cuts worsen the situation. The report recommends establishing a National Health Financing Forum, creating an ODA registry, introducing a health financing risk matrix, and reforming governance structures within the healthcare sector.

recent_articles.title: French minister says uncertain if hantavirus strain from cruise ship has mutated - World - DAWN.COM
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **French Health Minister Stephanie Rist** stated that the hantavirus strain on the **MV Hondius** cruise ship may have mutated, but officials remain "rather reassured" due to a lack of complete sequencing data. The outbreak has been linked to the Andes strain of hantavirus and is being investigated by **World Health Organisation**, which confirmed nine cases and urged isolation of suspected individuals. Italy's top infectious diseases hospital will examine biological samples from a man in quarantine who came into contact with a woman who died from the virus, but no further details were provided.

recent_articles.title: WHO head tells countries to prepare for more hantavirus cases | Hantavirus | The Guardian
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **World Health Organization** (WHO) has urged countries to prepare for more hantavirus cases following the outbreak aboard the MV Hondius cruise ship. The virus, which can be transmitted person-to-person in rare cases, has been confirmed in nine individuals, including a French woman and a US national who were evacuated from the ship. **Spain** played a crucial role in evacuating over 120 passengers and crew members, receiving praise from the WHO for its compassion and solidarity.  The UK is also preparing to bring 10 people from remote South Atlantic islands into the country for precautionary isolation. The WHO has acknowledged that more cases are likely due to interactions on board before preventative measures were taken.

recent_articles.title: ‘Unprecedented’ global effort gives new name to polycystic ovary syndrome – and new hope to millions of women | Polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS) | The Guardian
recent_articles.rephrased_article: After a decade of collaboration, **polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS)** has been renamed to polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS). The new name reflects the condition's broader impact on multiple systems in the body, including metabolism and risk of diabetes and cardiovascular disease.  The renaming was spearheaded by endocrinologist Prof Helena Teede, who emphasized that the term "polycystic" contributed to delayed diagnosis and inadequate medical care. Patients advocated for the change, highlighting the need for a name that better reflects the condition's complexity. The new name will be implemented in international guidelines for managing PCOS, with full implementation planned for 2028.

recent_articles.title: No sign of larger hantavirus outbreak, says UN health agency
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The World Health Organization (WHO)** has stated that there is "no sign" of a larger hantavirus outbreak after the evacuation of the last passengers from the disease-stricken cruise ship, **MV Hondius**.  **Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus**, head of the **WHO**, warned that the situation could change and more cases might emerge in the coming weeks. The ship is expected to arrive in Rotterdam on May 17th after a six-day voyage.  The final six passengers, including crew members from various countries, have been repatriated to their home countries.

recent_articles.title: Last passengers from hantavirus-hit ship evacuated; American tests positive | Health News | Al Jazeera
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The US Department of Health and Human Services (HHS)** announced that one of the 18 American passengers evacuated from the hantavirus-stricken cruise ship, **MV Hondius**, has tested positive for the respiratory infection. The last two evacuation flights carrying passengers and crew from the ship landed in the Netherlands, where the vessel will undergo disinfection.  The World Health Organization (WHO) maintains that the risk to the public remains low, but recommends a 42-day quarantine for all passengers.

recent_articles.title: Quest for a rare bird, a landfill visit, a deadly outbreak: How Leo Schilperoord became hantavirus 'patient zero' - The Times of India
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Leo Schilperoord**, a Dutch ornithologist, is confirmed as the patient zero in a deadly hantavirus outbreak aboard the **MV Hondius** cruise ship. Authorities suspect he contracted the virus from long-tailed pygmy rice rats carrying the Andes strain of hantavirus while birdwatching at a landfill outside Ushuaia, Argentina.  The couple's travels across South America and Sri Lanka prior to their arrival on the ship are believed to have exposed them to the virus. **Mirjam Schilperoord**, his wife, also died after experiencing symptoms of the illness during her journey. The outbreak led to the evacuation of passengers and crew from the ship, with 94 people repatriated to their home countries.
